messages:
Maria: heads up — ran PTQ int8 on new reranker candidate set, saw ndcg drop vs fp16: 0.812 -> 0.779
Sam: ouch, that's sizable. same holdout and seed?
Maria: yes same holdout (stratified by query length), fixed seed. curious — short queries seem worse.
Jonah: can you share the exact eval command? also what label source? crowd or internal judges?
Maria: command: `python eval.py --model rerank-v2 --quant ptq-int8 --holdout holdout_v2 --seed 42`
Maria: labels = crowd (2023 batch) + some small internal verification set
Kevin: label noise could explain some drop, especially if short queries have higher disagreement. any confusion matrix by query length?
Maria: quick numbers: short(<20 tokens) ndcg_fp16=.801 ndcg_int8=.741; mid(20-60) .824 -> .807; long(>60) .832 -> .828
Sam: that suggests PTQ hurting short-form. maybe KV-cache packing or tokenization differences at inference time
Jonah: also check candidate truncation order — if doc formatting changed after tokenization it will shift scores
Maria: good point. I noticed preproc used `join_with_newline=True` for docs in int8 docker image, while fp16 build uses a single-space join
Kevin: we should control for formatting and re-run with identical preproc
Maria: re-run queued. also planning bootstrap CI for ndcg delta: `python eval_bootstrap.py --iters 1000 --metric ndcg@10`
EvalBot: CI job 1680012360 started for rerank-v2 ptq-int8 holdout_v2
Sam: also consider running QAT or mixed-precision sweep — PTQ might be more brittle on that candidate distribution
Jonah: for stability check, can you swap labels: use internal-only and see if delta persists
Maria: will run internal-only next. ETA 30m
EvalBot: CI job 1680012405 finished — ndcg_fp16=.812 ndcg_int8=.779 delta=-0.033 (p~0.004 by bootstrap)
Kevin: p-value low, so likely real. next steps: 1) match preproc exactly 2) compare tokenization diffs 3) run QAT baseline
Sam: I'll help with tokenization parity test
Maria: thanks — I'll post results when the internal-only run completes :thumbsup:
Jonah: if we still see gap after parity, we should run small-scale QAT on top 4-bit base and compare
Maria: agreed. logging experiments to rerank/bringup-notes.md
Sam: nice. small ask — can we pin the candidate order in eval harness to avoid nondeterminism?
Maria: yes adding `--pin-order` flag to runs now
Kevin: booya :rocket:
